DIAGNOSIS: the search has converged and gen 8 produced the best signal in the archive on every dimension simultaneously — IntangibleYield_x_CashRichAndNotBurning (fmb 7.49, FF5 alpha 5.8%, t-alpha 6.18, Sharpe 0.52, coverage 0.142). Its structure is now the working answer: an intangible-adjusted operating profit yield, vetoed by the *weaker* of two financial-strength ranks, a cash stock and a cash-generation flow. The supporting evidence is coherent: cash stock alone t 5.49, cushion t 5.23, resources-only t 4.76, and the veto (MIN) form beats products of gates. Two channels are conclusively dead for alpha (own-history cash accumulation 0.7%, unrecorded capital intensity 1.6%, cushion dynamics 1.1%) despite strong Fama-MacBeth slopes — a reminder that fmb alone can mislead. The asset-backing anchor also failed on Sharpe (0.10) while retaining alpha, confirming the profit yield is the right valuation anchor. This final generation refines the winner along the three dimensions that remain genuinely open — how the flow leg should be measured, whether a third veto belongs, and whether the profit-yield anchor is essential — rather than exploring new territory.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: IntangibleYield_x_CashRich_PersistentGeneration
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(oiadp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho))), MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(che, at), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(MA(COALESCE(RATIO(oancf, at), RATIO(oiadp, at)), 3), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Whether a cash-rich cheap firm is a fortress or a melting ice cube depends on whether it generates cash reliably rather than in a single year, so smoothing the flow leg over three years should sharpen the veto by removing firms that had one good collection year and by rescuing firms with one transitory working-capital outflow.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The winning gate's flow leg is a one-year measurement of a slow-moving business property, and the archive has repeatedly shown that this family's alpha is driven by persistent rather than transitory quantities; a three-year average is the natural noise reduction and should raise t-alpha and Sharpe without touching coverage. It changes only the flow leg's horizon, so any improvement is unambiguously attributable.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: IntangibleYield_x_CashRich_AfterCapitalConsumption
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(oiadp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho))), MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(che, at), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(COALESCE(RATIO(SUB(oancf, dp), at), RATIO(oiadp, at)), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: A firm is only truly not burning cash if its operating cash flow also covers the consumption of its productive capital; charging depreciation against the flow leg makes the veto reflect free rather than gross cash generation, which is the correct test of whether the cash pile is sustainable.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This is the stricter economic definition of "not burning", and it addresses the critic's specific objection that the gross-cash-flow leg overlaps the archive's cash-return gates, since capital-intensive firms with high gross cash flow but full reinvestment needs now fail the veto. The accrual fallback is the exact analogue — operating profit already net of depreciation — so the construct is consistent across both samples and coverage stays at 0.14.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: IntangibleYield_x_ThreeDefectVeto
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(oiadp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho))), MIN(MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(che, at), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(COALESCE(RATIO(oancf, at), RATIO(oiadp, at)), 1))), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(COALESCE(RATIO(SUB(oiadp, oancf), at), RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(at, che), 1), DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1)), at)), 1)))))
HYPOTHESIS: A cheap firm must clear three independent hurdles to reprice — it must hold cash, generate cash, and report profit that is genuinely cash-backed — and because any one failure is sufficient to keep the discount open, the correct signal is the minimum of the three condition ranks.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The veto form has consistently outperformed multiplicative stacking in this archive (MIN of two gates 5.3% at t 5.13 versus a diluted triple product 3.8% at t 4.15 when a weak gate was multiplied in), and all three legs here are individually validated at t above 4. This is the maximal-evidence consolidation of everything learned, and its failure would be equally informative by showing that the accrual condition is already subsumed by the cash-strength conditions.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: IntangibleEnterpriseYield_x_CashRichAndNotBurning
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(oiadp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che)))), MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(che, at), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(COALESCE(RATIO(oancf, at), RATIO(oiadp, at)), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Pricing intangible-adjusted operating profit against enterprise value rather than equity value removes the leverage tilt from the valuation leg, so if the winning signal's alpha is genuine operating mispricing conditioned on financial strength it should survive — and become cleaner — under the capital-structure-neutral denominator.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The enterprise denominator improved the accrual-gated family (4.6% at t 3.71 versus 4.4% at t 4.12 for the equity version) but has never been paired with the veto gate that now dominates, and it matters for the final recommendation because an equity-yield signal conditioned on cash could be partly a disguised net-debt tilt. The one concern is that netting cash out of price overlaps the cash leg of the gate, which this test will quantify directly.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: IntangibleYield_x_CashRich_NotBurning_NotBorrowing
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(oiadp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho))), MIN(MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(che, at), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(COALESCE(RATIO(oancf, at), RATIO(oiadp, at)), 1))), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), at), 1)))))
HYPOTHESIS: A cash balance funded by fresh borrowing is not financial strength; only a cheap firm that holds cash, generates cash and did not increase its debt to do so is genuinely self-financing, and that combination is what the market under-prices.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This closes the one loophole in the winning gate — the cash stock is a level and says nothing about its source — using a debt-change term scaled by assets that is sign-safe and defined for debt-free firms, unlike the earlier growth-rate constructions. It also revisits the financing channel that failed as a payout composite (0.6%) in a form where the dividend term, which the critic showed dominated that test, is absent.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: BookToMarket_x_CashRichAndNotBurning
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(che, at), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(COALESCE(RATIO(oancf, at), RATIO(oiadp, at)), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: If financial strength is what makes cheapness pay, the veto should rescue the classic book-to-market anchor as well; if instead only profit-yield cheapness interacts with cash strength, then the mispricing is specifically about the price of earnings rather than about the price of assets.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Every book-to-market construction in this archive produced strong Fama-MacBeth slopes but zero FF5 alpha because HML spans them, and this is the decisive test of whether the veto gate is powerful enough to generate abnormal return from an HML-spanned value leg. The answer determines how we describe the final mechanism — a general "value works when the balance sheet is strong" claim versus the narrower and better-supported "cheap earnings pay when the firm holds and generates cash" claim.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---CRITIQUE IntangibleYield_x_CashRich_PersistentGeneration---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The expression is internally coherent and matches the hypothesis, but changing a single gate leg from a one-year to a three-year average is a pure horizon tweak on the archive's winning signal with no new economic content, and the archive's earlier smoothing precedent (NormalizedIntangibleEarningsYield, 3.7% at t 3.77 vs 4.4% at t 4.12) already suggests averaging dilutes rather than sharpens this family.

---CRITIQUE IntangibleYield_x_CashRich_AfterCapitalConsumption---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Charging depreciation against the flow leg is a defensible tightening of "not burning cash" and the oiadp fallback is genuinely the post-depreciation analogue, but the archive's earlier oancf−dp gate was the weakest of the cash-strength gates (t 1.38), so expected incremental gain over the winning veto is modest.

---CRITIQUE IntangibleYield_x_ThreeDefectVeto---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The MIN-of-three construction is consistent with the stated substitutes logic and each leg is individually validated, but the accrual leg (oiadp−oancf) is mechanically anti-correlated with the cash-generation leg (oancf/at), so the third hurdle is likely largely redundant and the test's main value is diagnostic rather than incremental alpha.

---CRITIQUE IntangibleEnterpriseYield_x_CashRichAndNotBurning---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 4
RATIONALE: This is a substantive capital-structure-neutrality test of the dominant veto signal rather than a cosmetic variant, the expression matches the hypothesis, and the proposal correctly pre-identifies the one real confound (cash appears in both the EV denominator and the cash leg), which makes the outcome interpretable either way.

---CRITIQUE IntangibleYield_x_CashRich_NotBurning_NotBorrowing---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The debt-change leg is sign-safe, well-scaled and addresses a genuine loophole (source of the cash stock), but it is close to the well-documented net-debt-issuance/external-financing anomaly and the archive's one prior test of this financing channel produced near-zero alpha, so the incremental prior is weak even though the isolation of the debt term from the dividend term is a fair follow-up.

---CRITIQUE BookToMarket_x_CashRichAndNotBurning---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: Book-to-market screened on cash holdings and cash generation is essentially the long-published Piotroski-style fundamental-strength screen within value stocks, and the archive has repeatedly shown B/M legs here yield strong FMB slopes with zero FF5 alpha because HML spans them, so the proposal is a rediscovery whose expected outcome the author already concedes is null.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: IntangibleYield_x_CashRich_ProductiveCoreBusiness
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(oiadp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho))), MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(che, at), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(COALESCE(RATIO(oancf, SUB(at, che)), RATIO(oiadp, SUB(at, che))), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: The two conditions in the winning veto are currently measured against the same base, so a large cash pile mechanically depresses the flow leg and partially cancels the very strength it is meant to confirm; measuring cash generation per dollar of *operating* (non-cash) assets makes the two tests economically independent and states the correct condition — cash held alongside a core business that actually earns on its own capital.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: This is not a horizon tweak but a correction of a mechanical anti-correlation between the two veto legs: cash sits in the numerator of one and inflates the denominator of the other, so the winning gate systematically understates the strength of exactly the cash-rich firms it selects. Removing cash from the flow leg's capital base is also the economically right going-concern test, it was independently productive in the archive as a standalone gate (3.5% at t 2.98 despite only 0.09 coverage), and the accrual fallback keeps the sample at 0.14.
---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: GrossProfitYield_x_CashRichAndNotBurning
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), MUL(prcc_f, csho))), MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(che, at), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(COALESCE(RATIO(oancf, at), RATIO(oiadp, at)), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Gross profit is measured before overheads, R&D and depreciation, so it is immune to the expensing and capitalization choices that our intangible addback and accrual gate were built to correct; if the veto still generates alpha on a gross-profit anchor, the mechanism is the pricing of a firm's fundamental earning power conditioned on financial strength rather than an artifact of any particular accounting adjustment.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: This replaces the book-to-market test — which the critic rightly identified as an HML-spanned rediscovery whose null result we already anticipated — with an anchor that is a genuine profit yield, is not spanned by HML, and deliberately strips out every accounting item the winning specification manipulates. It is therefore the sharpest available robustness check on the final recommendation: a comparable alpha establishes that the result does not depend on the intangible correction, while a materially weaker one tells us the overhead and intangible adjustments in the numerator are doing real work.
